items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And everybody in our new band... Well Cat Daddy is a professional runner.

ctx.x: He could have gone broke if he had to pay royalties to all the fellows that he took licks from.
Snooky had certain things, Curtis Peagler had his certain thing, and naturally Cat Daddy and Ricky Woodard, he had his certain thing. You’d always know it’s Ricky because you hear this thing.
Yeah. Once you hear it, oh, that’s Ricky.

items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: In our new band now we have Ricky Woodard, we have Nolan Shaheed, we have Richard Reid on bass.

ctx.x: And he walks around in their heads.

And he knows. And that’s where he’s such a valuable accompanist. And I could see why Carmen McRae would love him, see because we worked with her too. But he’s the last one of the old band. In our new band now we have Ricky Woodard, we have Nolan Shaheed, we have Richard Reid on bass. We call him “Roughouse.” And we express to the audience, if you don’t behave we’re going to let Richard Reid fall on you.
I take it he’s a fairly big man.
